Figure 1. CYP450-catalyzed oxidative coupling reactions and structures and chemical transformations of piperazine skeleton. a) CYP450-catalyzed
dimerization formation of biaryl compounds through C� C bond linkage. b) CYP450-catalyzed generation of dimeric DKP family alkaloids through
C� C or C� N bond formation, respectively. c) Structure of piperazine and representative drugs and natural products with a piperazine moiety. d)
The well-known CYP450-catalyzed intramolecular oxidative coupling formation of more complex piperazine-derived scaffolds; however, the
intermolecular oxidative coupling of the piperazine skeleton was not discovered to date.

natural products. a) The clade of fungal CYP450 dimerases including

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Confirmation of the function of CpsA, B, E and F. a) LC–MS analysis of the culture extracts from AN-cpsA and AN-cpsAB. b) Proposed
pathways for the formation of 1–4a/4b. c) LC–MS analysis of the culture extracts from different gene combination of cpsAB with cpsC/D/E/F in A.
nidulans, respectively. d) Compounds 4a/4b are N13-acyl atropisomers according to NOESY analysis.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Investigation of the function and proposed catalytic mechanism of CYP450 CpsD. a) LC–MS analysis of the culture extracts from different
gene combinations in A. nidulans. b) Structures of natural and artificial substrates and products. c) Two proposed mechanisms for CpsD-catalyzed
oxidative coupling reactions. d) The in vitro biochemical assays of CpsD towards natural and artificial substrates.
